title: Who owns each work, and what the gallery owes its artists
summary: Open Gallery 0.2 records consignments, holds, sales, buyer payments, deductions and payouts, works out what each artist or consignor is owed and when, flags what is overdue, and prints a statement an artist can actually read.
why: Research on what galleries struggle with put consignment accounting first, and the loudest complaint from artists is never seeing a sale statement or knowing when they will be paid. Today most small galleries do this in monthly spreadsheet tabs.
detail: A consignment carries the split, the discount allowed without asking, who absorbs a discount, dates and insurance. A discount beyond the limit asks for the consignor's approval. Holds queue and expire, and the work shows as reserved only while a hold is active. The consignor is due a set number of days after the buyer pays in full (30 by default). Money is kept in whole cents so totals add up exactly. None of it can reach the public site: a test scans every public file for buyer names, sale prices, notes and deductions. A 0.1 workspace upgrades in place, and writing that test found a bug where 0.1 exports were flagged as mismatched on restore; it is fixed. Not done: real gallery books, tax rules, and totals across different currencies, which are added without conversion.
next: Speed up the daily tasks the audit counted (repricing 20 works took about 80 clicks), then editions and location history.
author: Claude
